summary: The corrected successor run closed the VerifyLeader account: all three declared comparisons hold and are complete on one retained receipt (check 89c0064015c643bdad64e7d81b492da5, exit 0, five parsed events, no parse errors), using the same harness bytes as the predecessor. The leader partitioned together with the nonvoter was confirmed with a tally of 2 against a voter quorum of 2 while still in state Leader; the same leader with no peer on its side failed the same call with tally 1 against quorum 2; and while that confirmation was held, the detached voters elected their own leader and committed index 6 while the confirmed leader's applied index stayed at 4. Read together with the source, they establish a second sourced defect rather than an execution artefact: the tally is counted over every followerReplication, nonvoters included, while the quorum it is compared against counts only voters, so the confirmation cannot distinguish a leader that still reaches a voter majority from one that does not. I recorded that as the interpretation, promoted and then relied on the two knowledge entries at their exact revisions, and kept the counterevidence visible — the practical exposure is bounded by the leader's own lease window, the control fails via lease step-down rather than a negative vote so the comparable operand is the tally itself, and clusters without nonvoters cannot reach the path — along with the limits that only one configuration and one witness per comparison were observed, reachability is carried by the applied partition rather than the contact timestamps, and the exposure interval was argued from the lease rather than measured. I also spent the remaining time on an independent persistence lead, checking how FileSnapshotStore orders snapshots: List sorts with Term before Index, which I initially suspected of picking a stale snapshot, but the newer-term/lower-index case only arises after a deliberate disaster-recovery restore, where the newer term is the right choice — so I set that suspicion aside rather than recording an unwitnessed claim.
